patch_description:
The current approach uses one exponentially weighted endpoint fit with fixed decay (2.85), alpha range 0.18–0.68, beta range 0.012–0.097, and a single innovation-based reversal check. This can still allow unstable local slopes and endpoint spikes to generate frequent directional changes.

The new configuration separates observation, state tracking, and reversal confirmation. It uses: (1) robust full-window and recent-window endpoint regressions, (2) one Huber residual-reweighting pass, (3) additional newest-sample contradiction downweighting when an endpoint spike opposes both fitted slope and confirmed direction, (4) confidence-weighted blending of long and short horizon measurements, and (5) a two-sample reversal confirmation gate with a large-event bypass. Lower baseline gains improve smoothness and false-reversal suppression, while coherent multi-scale slope agreement and high-curvature conditions increase gains to preserve responsiveness at genuine turns.
